pieces.text: Cells can make exact copies of their genetic information because DNA's double-stranded structure allows it to act as a template for its own replication. Each DNA molecule is composed of two nucleotide strands held together by hydrogen bonds. These hydrogen bonds form between specific pairs of nitrogenous bases—adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T), and cytosine (C) pairs with guanine (G). Because of this
, each of the two DNA strands contains the information necessary to exactly replicate the other strand.
